correctness.rationale: The statement follows from four exactly derived conditional drifts (S, X, C, cubic U), explicit harmonic summation, an L2-bounded nondegenerate degree-square martingale, and two martingale Cesàro transfers. E U_n=O(n^(3/2)) makes the relevant innovation-weight variance series summable, proving a.s. and L2 convergence. All finite-size constants and state recurrences were independently checked by exact-rational exhaustive enumeration through nine vertices (184,947 assertions). Finite checks are not claimed to prove the infinite theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A sum over arbitrarily large leaf-child counts, growing at n log n with a nondegenerate random n-scale correction, is not a count of a single fixed finite fringe shape. General additive-functional machinery could conceivably provide implicit coverage; see residual risks.

originality.rationale: The present claim gives an exact finite-n count expectation and an order-n almost-sure/L2 random limit for a globally unbounded sum of common-parent leaf pairs. The recent local leafdegree-distribution theorem, cherry-based symmetry arguments, and fixed finite fringe-shape CLTs examined do not imply this statement. Six real semantic research-record queries and targeted public literature searches found no covering claim. This is best-knowledge original with explicit residual historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The global sibling-leaf pair count is a natural motif/symmetry invariant. The known leafdegree tail ell^(-3) makes the unbounded quadratic leafdegree census a critical logarithmic observable not controlled by fixed-ell limit laws. The exact n log n coefficient and nondegenerate order-n random correction identify a mathematically significant transition from fixed finite fringe counts and connect it to the quadratic-degree martingale; exact finite-size expectations support further work.
